transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-06
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Daniel Kim (Redwood SE), Sofia Alvarez (Channel Ops - Redwood); Priya Ramesh (NovaScale Head of Partnerships), Liam O'Connor (NovaScale Head of GTM), Jesse Tan (NovaScale Sales Enablement)

Summary:
- Handoff of co-sell pipeline from NovaScale to Redwood; align on motion, lead routing, and revenue split.
- Decide technical validation plan (Dedicated baseline) and documentation needs (SOC2, SSO, KMS).
- Agree next steps: joint deck, enablement cadence, and pilot / proof milestones.

Topics discussed:
1) Current pipeline and hot deals (what's at risk/close timeline)
2) GTM motion: who owns outbound vs inbound; lead routing rules
3) Technical concerns: VPC/private deploy, SOC2, KMS, latency SLOs
4) Commercials: referral vs co-sell split; attribution and contract handoff
5) Enablement: joint training, battlecards, case studies

Action items (recap in call): see metadata action_items list above

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Okay hi everyone, thanks for hopping on. We're running about 50 minutes, agenda is pipeline handoff and a quick strategy on how we co-sell the next set of accounts. Priya, do you want to kick us off with the pipeline health?

[00:18] Priya (NovaScale): Yeah, sure. Thanks. So high level — we have five active opportunities that we're prioritizing for joint outreach. Two of them are at legal review but both flagged as Q2 closes, one is POC stage, another is discovery with customer infra teams, and one is a low touch SMB play. I'm mostly here to make sure the handoff to Redwood's AE/SE is clean and to surface any technical blockers up front.

[00:42] Liam (NovaScale): Most of the enterprise ones will require either Dedicated or a VPC/private deploy because of data residency. They asked about SOC 2, SSO/SAML, and KMS support. Also timeline — legal usually needs two to four weeks once we provide the security pack.

[01:05] Daniel (Redwood SE): Got it. Real quick on the Dedicated option — Dedicated gives us reserved GPU pools and isolation, which helps with throughput and compliance. For the latency numbers, I can run a baseline using a small subset of their logs. It helps to set expectations.

[01:22] Jesse (NovaScale): Quick Q: when you say "baseline," what's the typical thing you run? Are you simulating tokens, or do you need their prompt set?

[01:30] Daniel: Ideally a representative prompt set and a sample — 500 to 2k examples — we run steady-state throughput and p95/p99 latency. If you can't share real data, a synthetic distribution that's representative helps. We'll annotate the results with sequence lengths and KV cache behavior.

[01:52] Priya: We can do a sanitized export for the POC customer. Note: legal will want to see SOC2 Type II report, KMS proof, and the VPC diagram.

[02:04] Maya: Perfect. Sofia, are we tracking a partner enablement timeline? I want to make sure the NovaScale reps have the battlecards.

[02:12] Sofia (Redwood): Yes — we're prepping a partner enablement pack. It includes: joint deck, 2-page co-sell one-pager, battlecards for competitive knockouts, an intro script for AE cold reach, and a shared pipeline template. I'll push the enablement calendar after this call.

[02:30] Liam: On revenue split — NovaScale historically does a referral fee for inbound leads, but for co-sell where both teams actively pursue, we usually do a 50/50 (net new) or 30/70 depending on who owns the contract. We need a written framework so ops can automate payables.

[02:47] Maya: For Redwood, we prefer an uplift on the standard referral for active co-sells; typically we try to be flexible — can we draft a proposal and loop in legal?

[02:58] Priya: Yes. I'll coordinate with legal. I think the important part is the attribution window and primary owner rules.

[03:12] Jesse: Also need clarity on who handles renewal conversations — is it NovaScale or Redwood?

[03:18] Maya: Good point. Usually retention is owned by Redwood, but NovaScale will get credited for renewal touches if they have the relationship. We can define it in the deal handoff doc.

[03:30] [Crosstalk — someone shuffling papers]

[03:45] Daniel: Technical note — there are two things we often recommend on partner POCs: 1) run a small Dedicated baseline to prove latency and throughput, 2) set up a short-lived Private demo in a VPC for the security reviewers to inspect logs and networking. That second one can be air-gapped-like for the duration of evaluation.

[04:06] Priya: That helps. For the biggest deal, the infra team insisted on HSM-backed KMS. Do you support HSM integration?

[04:13] Daniel: We support customer-managed keys and integrate with most KMS/HSM providers via standard APIs. We'll need to capture the exact provider and exchange connectivity docs. Also note: depending on the quantization and model variant, disclosed performance numbers can change a bit.

[04:31] Liam: Speaking of models — does Redwood provide model verification reports? The procurement team often asks for performance profiles and token cost estimates.

[04:40] Maya: Yes, we have model catalog profiles and a perf sheet for common sequence lengths. I'll attach the perf-to-cost estimator in the deck. Note that we can also propose batching and caching recommendations via Redwood Optimize to reduce cost.

[04:58] Priya: Excellent. For the pipeline handoff, we want a simple doc that says: lead source, whether it's co-sell or referral, expected ARR, close date, primary owner, current stage, blockers. Can Redwood map that into your CRM?

[05:15] Maya: We can. If you send the CSV or use the shared Google sheet we'll ingest the rows and create opportunities. Also we'll annotate with Redwood owner and SE notes.

[05:28] Jesse: Are we using a shared spreadsheet for attribution? In the past we had mismatches because the CRM timestamps differ.

[05:36] Sofia: We'll add a unique partner pipeline id per row to make sure attribution is deterministic. That id will be included in email threads and in the CRM.

[05:46] Priya: Ok that should help. On the enablement side, can Redwood provide a quick 30-minute training for NovaScale AEs next Thursday?

[05:54] Maya: Yes, we can do a focused 30-minute session: product overview (10 min), integration/pilot ask (10 min), and closing playbook (10 min). I can schedule that after we finalize the deck.

[06:07] Liam: Let's talk about lead routing rules — our preference is that inbound web leads go to NovaScale first for discovery, and if they convert to an enterprise opportunity, we loop in Redwood AE. Outbound joint motions will be co-owned. How do we configure that?

[06:22] Sofia: We'll build a routing doc: rule table like "lead type -> owner" plus SLA for response times. We can also add automated notifications to NovaScale Slack channel.

[06:33] Maya: Also important — case prioritization for POCs. We need SLAs on support (e.g., SE support within 24 hours for POC blockers). That will be in the enablement/ops packet.

[06:45] Priya: Legal and procurement — what docs can you share now so we can start review?

[06:50] Daniel: We can share SOC 2 Type II summary, a redacted VPC diagram, standard DPA, and our KMS integration notes. I can drop those in the shared folder by end of day.

[07:02] [Sound of keyboard; brief silence]

[07:18] Jesse: Pricing question — for the SMB low-touch deal, which is more price-sensitive, do you have a simple hosted plan we can offer?

[07:25] Maya: Yes, for SMB we usually propose the hosted API with per-token pricing and an optional dedicated connector. For cost-sensitive customers we suggest quantized model variants and stronger caching — Redwood Optimize will provide recommendations. We should ensure NovaScale reps have the per-token estimates per use-case.

[07:40] Liam: For enterprise, can Redwood support custom SLAs on latency? Some of our customers require <200ms p95 for short seqs.

[07:48] Daniel: With Dedicated plus tuning we can meet aggressive p95 numbers for shorter sequences; when sequence lengths balloon the p99 will move. We'll document expectations in the perf sheet and call out trade-offs.

[08:04] Priya: Good — that helps the procurement conversations.

[08:10] Maya: Quick runway question — what's your expected close window for the top 2 deals?

[08:14] Priya: One is legal review (target close 2025-05-30), the other is a POC completing mid-June (target close 2025-06-20). The rest are Q3.

[08:24] Maya: Okay. We'll prioritize the legal-review deal for fast-tracking paperwork and the POC for the Dedicated baseline.

[08:31] [Minor phone notification beep]

[08:45] Daniel: On the POC, I recommend we define exit criteria — e.g., p95 < 400ms on the client workload and <2x the expected token cost. We should write that into the POC success criteria so procurement has a measurable bar.

[08:57] Jesse: That's helpful. We'll add those to the POC plan.

[09:05] Maya: For the joint deck — I'll include: partnership overview, co-sell motion, joint value prop, example ROI calc, and a page with technical checklist (SOC2, KMS, VPC diagram). Any must-have slides from NovaScale?

[09:18] Priya: A slide that explains how NovaScale routes leads, and one with our channel contacts and escalation path. Also a short case study of a previous co-sell win would be great.

[09:30] Sofia: We'll also provide a two-page one-pager targeted at procurement: SSO, DPA, SOC2, and support contact.

[09:40] Liam: For the revenue share mechanics — can we run a small spreadsheet example: ARR $180k, NovaScale receives 20% if referral, 40% if co-sell? We need clarity on when to pay out.

[09:54] Maya: We'll draft the sample payout scenarios and include it in the partner agreement template.

[10:02] [Short lull while someone types]

[10:20] Daniel: I'll also note technical caveats — model choice, quantization, and KV cache will change throughput and cost. For transparency we'll provide two scenario tables: conservative and optimistic.

[10:35] Priya: That will help us manage expectations with customers.

[10:42] Maya: Anything else on the pipeline itself? Anyone worried about deal slippage?

[10:48] Priya: The legal-review deal had a procurement delay earlier in the quarter; if we can accelerate the DPA review that should help.

[10:56] Maya: We'll mark that deal as "Legal Fast-Track" and assign a priority.

[11:04] Jesse: One more item — enablement materials for NovaScale reps: can we get 3 battlecards for common objections: 1) latency/cost tradeoff, 2) security/compliance, 3) price comparisons vs Anthropic/OpenAI?

[11:18] Sofia: Yep. We'll produce short battlecards and a cheat sheet.

[11:26] Liam: Can we sync on metrics to report weekly? NovaScale needs a simple dashboard with: # of co-sell leads, pipeline ARR, conversion %, and number of POCs started.

[11:36] Maya: We'll populate a partner dashboard in the console and share a weekly snapshot.

[11:45] Priya: Great. How will leads be tracked operationally — email, shared sheet, or CRM?

[11:50] Sofia: The canonical source will be the shared pipeline sheet; we will push rows into CRM and keep a synced copy for visibility.

[12:00] Maya: All right, quick recap and owners: Maya to send the joint deck and per-token estimator (due 2025-05-09). Daniel to run Dedicated baseline and drop results (due 2025-05-14). Sofia to send enablement pack and schedule 30-min training (due 2025-05-11). Priya to connect channel ops and confirm lead CSV (due 2025-05-10).

[12:30] Priya: That all sounds good. We'll make the intros tomorrow.

[12:36] Maya: Perfect. We'll follow up in email with the shared links (I'll include the perf sheet and security docs). Anything else?

[12:44] Liam: No, thanks everyone. Looking forward to the pilot.

[12:48] Maya: Thanks all. We'll close out with the action items and schedule the enablement session.

[12:55] [Call ends]

Notes / references: shared deck link (placeholder): https://redwood.company/shared/decks/novascale-cosell-v1, shared pipeline sheet: https://sheets.shared/novascale-redwood-pipeline (access by invite).

End of transcript.
